thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2/g4' reporting sustained p99 generation latency > 12s and streaming stalls for last 9m. Queue depth rising > 420. autoscaler:scale_up events failing due to warmup timeout.

alex: saw it, joining. p95 also creeping but p99 is worst.

morgan: confirmed on dashboards — P99 spiked to ~14.2s at 1957765380. streaming stalls correlate with KV cache misses.

sam: queue depth backpressure visible on router metrics: q_len per-shard ~> 120. autoscaler logs show warmup timeouts on several pods: 'warmup exceeded 60s' then pod terminated.

vivian: customer impact? any active SLAs tripped?

alex: several customers on Dedicated with higher priority routes impacted. No full outages but tail latency SLOs breached for ~8 customers (reported by alerting rules).

leo: initial mitigation idea: manual scale up of pool, increase min replicas, enable fallback model routing for streaming clients, and shed low-priority batch requests.

alex: doing manual scale now — running the control-plane command to add 4 nodes to the pool.

alex: command: ```redwoodctl pool resize --pool eu-west-2/g4 --add 4 --reason "incident 1957765432"```

deploy-bot: notice: resize request acknowledged, provisioning 4 warmup instances (IDs: i-0a1b2c3d i-0d4c3b2a i-0f1e2d3c i-0c3b2a1d). Warmup started. ETA ~ 50-70s each.

morgan: autoscaler config looks aggressive on warmup_timeout (60s). We hit a pathological pattern: rapid burst -> autoscaler tries to add capacity -> warmup not finished before router sends traffic -> pods drop or error -> more autoscale -> chicken-egg.

sam: we should throttle router's routing to new pods until warmup complete. There's a flag to mark instances as 'ready-for-routing' only after warmup healthcheck passes. Can we flip that temporarily?

alex: yes, enabling strict readiness gating, and also increasing warmup_timeout to 120s for the pool to avoid premature termination. Running config update now: ```redwoodctl pool update --pool eu-west-2/g4 --warmup-timeout 120 --readiness-gate strict```

vivian: also start routing non-streaming traffic to fallback smaller model variant (quantized) to reduce GPU memory and shorten warmup. Need a rollout plan.

leo: creating a quick routing rule: curl to control plane:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" 
  https://control-plane.internal/v1/routing/override 
  -d '{"selector":"app:streaming","action":"route-to","model":"gpt-small-quantized-v2","ttl":900}'
```

deploy-bot: routing override applied for selector app:streaming -> gpt-small-quantized-v2 (ttl 900s).

morgan: good. that should reduce warmup pressure. we still need to handle queued requests: suggest enabling queue-shedding for non-critical routes (response: 503 with retry-after) to preserve capacity for streaming sessions.

sam: enabling queue-shedding policy now. Command: ```redwoodctl queue update --pool eu-west-2/g4 --policy shed-low-priority --threshold 200```

alex: putting customer comms in motion. Opening incident page and notifying affected accounts with ETA.

alex: Incident page: https://status.internal/incidents/1957765432 — added current impact, mitigation steps, and ETA for SLO recovery ~15-25m.

vivian: monitoring metrics: p99 trending down to ~7.5s after routing override and initial scale events. queue depth beginning to fall (now ~260).

morgan: warmup successes starting at 1957765560 for two instances, third one at 1957765605. We should see steady improvements in next 5-10m.

sam: noting a streaming-specific issue: some streaming connections show 'stall at token 1' logs — looks like KV cache priming failing when route changed. Patch: add short prefetch pass for active sessions to prime KV after routing switch.

leo: rolling a small config to enable KV prefetch on fallback model for active sessions. Patch command: ```redwoodctl feature-toggle set kv-prefetch-on-routing true --scope pool:eu-west-2/g4```

deploy-bot: feature toggle applied.

alex: quick check on costs: temporary scale + fallback routing will increase spend — OK for now, prioritize customer impact. We'll follow up on cost remediation post-incident.

vivian: preparing pager handoff notes for next oncall in 30m: summarize alerts, what we changed (manual scale + warmup timeout + readiness gating + routing override + queue-shedding), remaining actions (observe traffic, revert routing after steady-state, adjust autoscaler policy).

morgan: creating a checklist in the incident page. Also adding runbook items: increase autoscaler warmup_timeout in steady config, add readiness gating by default for new pool types, and adjust backoff logic to avoid oscillation during bursts.

sam: observed one failing machine with repeated GPU driver error during warmup: 'nvml: driver response timeout'. Marking host for postmortem and repro.

leo: capturing logs snippet: ```
[1957765499] warmup: container start
[1957765560] warmup: healthcheck failed - nvml: driver response timeout
[1957765565] warmup: terminated and replaced
```

alex: customer update sent. Slack DM from cs-team: "some customers reporting degraded streaming experience — appreciate update."

vivian: current statuses: p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~5.8s (improving), queue depth ~140, warmup complete on all 4 added instances. Still watching KV-prefetch errors but reduced stalls.

morgan: closing immediate paging. switching to monitoring-only. oncall handoff to night shift @oncall-rotation in 30m. add a follow-up to run a post-incident RCA and adjust autoscaler parameters.

alex: agreed. Handoff note: 
- Incident start: 1957765432 (alert)
- Impact: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2/g4' p99 generation SLO breached for ~9 customers, streaming stalls observed
- Mitigations applied: manual pool scale + readiness gating + warmup_timeout increased to 120s + route fallback to quantized model + queue-shedding for low-priority requests + KV prefetch toggle
- Current state: latency improving, p99 trending below SLO, queue draining
- Next actions: RCA (assign to infra/serving), fix failing host driver, tune autoscaler warmup/backoff, revert routing override during steady-state

oncall-rotation: taking it from here. thanks team. I'll monitor overnight and escalate if regressions.

alex: thanks everyone — great coordination. closing this thread once RCA ticket created.

morgan: created ticket INFRA-4921 for RCA and follow-ups. Linking to incident page.

deploy-bot: incident update logged, channel archived pending postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to S2 at 1957766120 — monitoring mode.

alex: thread closed for active paging. leave comments on incident page for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
